source_text: Πολλῷ δὲ τούτου βελτίους οἳ κοινωνίαν ἅμα βίου ἐστείλαντο, ἐξ ἧς καρποῖντο ἂν τὰ βέλτιστα; Δύο γὰρ ἀνδρῶν τοῖς αὐτοῖς πράγμασιν ὀρθῶς προσκειμένων, εἰ καὶ θατέρῳ τινὶ προσπέσῃ τι· ἀλλὰ μὴν οὐ μικρὰν ἐπικουρίαν ἔχει, τὸν αὐτῷ συνόντα. Μεγίστη δὲ καὶ συμφορὰ ἀνθρώπῳ δυσπραγοῦντι, καὶ ἡ ἐρημία τοῦ ἀνακτησομένου. Οἱ δ᾽ αὖ ὁμοδίαιτοι, καὶ τὴν εὐπραγίαν αὐτοῖς ἐδιπλασίασαν, καὶ πραγμάτων ἀβουλήτων χειμῶνα παρεμυθήσαντο· ὥστε καὶ μεθημέραν τῇ ἐπ᾽ ἀλλήλοις λαμπρύνεσθαι παρρησίᾳ, καὶ νύκτωρ φαιδρότητι σεμνύνεσθαι. Ὁ δὲ βίον ἀκοινώνητον ἕλκων, φρικώδη τινὰ ἑαυτῷ διεξάγει ζωήν, οὐκ ᾐσθημένος, ὡς εἰ καὶ ἐπίθοιτό τις ἀνθρώποις συμπεφραγμένοις, θρασέως καὶ οὐκ ἀσφαλῶς βουλεύεται, καὶ ὅτι οὐδὲ σχοῖνος τριπλῇ ῥᾳδίως ἀπορρήγνυσθαι πέφυκεν. Ἐγὼ δὲ προκρίνω νέον πένητα σώφρονα, γέροντος βασιλέως ἄφρονος, ᾧ ἐνθύμιον οὐ γεγένηται, ὡς δυνατόν ἐστι, τῶν μὲν ἐκ τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου τινὰ εἰς τὸ βασιλεῦσαι καταστῆναι, αὐτὸν δὲ τῆς ἀδίκου δυναστείας, δικαίως ὕστερον ἐκπεσεῖν. Συμβαίνει γὰρ τοὺς ὑπὸ τῷ νέῳ μέν, ἔμφρονι δὲ τασσομένους, ἀλύπους εἶναι τοὺς ὅσοι προγενέστεροι. Οἱ γὰρ μετέπειτα γενόμενοι, διὰ τὸ ἑτέρου ἀπειράτως ἔχειν, οὐδὲ τοῦτον ἐπαινεῖν δύνανται, ἀγόμενοί τε γνώμῃ ἀλογίστῳ, καὶ ὁρμῇ πνεύματος ἐναντίου. Ἐκκλησιάζων δὲ πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν ἔχε τόν τ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ βίον ὀρθῶς διαπορεύεσθαι, καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀφρόνων εὔχεσθαι, ὅπως ἐπίσταιντο σύνεσιν λαβόντες, ἐκκλίνειν τὴν πρᾶξιν τῶν πονηρῶν.
thought_title: Two are better than one; the wise poor youth
orientation: Partnership is better than a solitary life, and a sensible poor youth is better than a foolish old king.
pass_a_gloss: Much better than this one are those who together equipped, undertook a partnership of life, from which they would reap the best things (printed with a question mark). For of two men rightly applying themselves to the same affairs, even if something should befall one of the two, yet indeed he has no small help, the one being with him. And greatest calamity for a man faring badly is also the desolation, lack of one who will restore him. But those living together both doubled the prosperity for themselves, and consoled the winter, storm of unwished affairs; so that by day they are made brilliant by the frankness, confidence toward one another, and by night they are dignified by cheerfulness. But the one dragging an unshared life passes through for himself a shuddering, dreadful life, not having perceived that, if anyone should attack men fenced together, he plans boldly and not safely, and that not even a threefold rope is by nature easily broken off. But I prefer a poor young man of sound mind to an old senseless king, to whom it has not become a consideration that it is possible for one of those from the prison to be appointed to reign, and for himself to fall out later, justly, from the unjust power. For it happens that those ranked under the young but sensible one, as many as were born earlier, are without grief. For those who came to be afterwards, because of being without experience of the other, cannot even praise this one, being led by an unreasoning judgment and by an impulse of a contrary, hostile spirit. But while taking part in the assembly, have before your eyes both to pass through your own life rightly, and to pray on behalf of the senseless, so that, having received understanding, they might know how to turn aside from the practice of wicked things.

pass_b_english: Far better than he are those who have joined their lives in partnership, from which they may reap the best of fruits (Ecclesiastes 4:9). For when two men rightly devote themselves to the same affairs, even if some mishap befalls one of them, he still has no small help in the one who is with him; but for a man in trouble the greatest misfortune is to have no one to lift him up again (Ecclesiastes 4:10). Those who share a common life, on the other hand, double their good fortune and comfort each other through the winter of unwelcome events, so that by day they shine with the confidence they have in one another, and by night they are graced with gladness (Ecclesiastes 4:11). But the man who drags out a solitary life leads a grim existence for himself, never realizing that anyone who attacks men who stand close together makes a rash and unsafe plan, and that a threefold cord does not easily break (Ecclesiastes 4:12).

I prefer a poor young man of sound mind to an old and foolish king (Ecclesiastes 4:13), who never took it to heart that it is possible for someone from prison to be set up as king, and for himself to fall in the end, and justly, from his unjust power (Ecclesiastes 4:14). For it turns out that all those of the older generation who are placed under the young but sensible ruler live free from grief (Ecclesiastes 4:15). For those born afterward, having no experience of the other, cannot praise even this one, led as they are by thoughtless judgment and by the drive of a hostile spirit (Ecclesiastes 4:16).

When you take part in the assembly, keep this before your eyes: to walk the path of your own life rightly, and to pray for the foolish, that they may receive understanding and know how to turn away from doing evil (Ecclesiastes 5:1).
notes: Paraphrase of Ecclesiastes 4:9-16 and 5:1. Versification: the last sentence renders LXX/Hebrew Ecclesiastes 4:17, which is English Ecclesiastes 5:1; it is cited by the English number. The first sentence is printed with a question mark after τὰ βέλτιστα; a question introduced by a relative clause makes poor Greek, so it is rendered as a statement (sense unchanged). 'Winter' keeps χειμῶνα ('winter, storm'), which ties the image to the warmth of 4:11. 'A grim existence' renders φρικώδη ζωήν (a shuddering, dreadful life). 'Of sound mind' renders σώφρονα, where the verse has 'wise'. 'Those of the older generation' renders τοὺς ὅσοι προγενέστεροι; 4:15-16 is condensed by Gregory, and the clause is cited to 4:15. 'When you take part in the assembly' renders ἐκκλησιάζων (the verb Solomon used of himself in section 1); it answers 'when you go to the house of God' in the verse. The source row records one correction (ὅτι for ὄτι in the threefold-cord clause), already printed.
